source.title: Rethink the Connections among Generalization, Memorization, and the Spectral Bias of DNNs
source.authors: Xiao Zhang; Haoyi Xiong; Dong-Rui Wu

record.tranche_reason: The study varies label noise and reports training and test error behavior, refining the expectation that more memorization of noise leads to steadily worsening test error. It does not test the fully random-label, unstructured-input, regularization, or learning-order claims.
record.gate_note: Results cited from Zhang et al. (2017) and Arpit et al. (2017) are prior work, not this study's results. Figure 2 reports errors for 10% label noise; Appendix A Figure 8 shows spectra, not errors, for 20% noise. Figure-only error values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study tests V6 in an extended-training setting: Section 2.2 explicitly reports that test error initially falls while perturbed-label error remains high, followed by noise memorization. Its fixed-noise learning curves do not test V4's relationship between corruption fraction and test error. Epoch-wise double descent does not contradict that relationship.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: high-frequency components can diminish late in training while corrupted points remain memorized, alongside a second descent in test error. The authors also propose training-set spectra as indicators of the second descent. Their spectral result does not refute the observed ordering of pattern learning before noise memorization.
record.recipe_differences: Uses partially shuffled training labels and extended training, then analyzes local Fourier spectra and test-error curves; it does not reproduce the full-random-label experiments in the cited sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture are varied; label noise is 10% in Figure 2 and 0% and 20% in Appendix A spectrum plots. The authors also report that skip connections influence spectra.

fits_no_version.finding: Test error improves again during extended training while corrupted training points remain memorized.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed label corruption, continued training can improve generalization after noise memorization through epoch-wise double descent.

fits_no_version.finding: Late-training high-frequency components diminish off the training manifold while corrupted points remain memorized.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral complexity need not increase monotonically during training, even when label noise remains memorized.

record.peer_reviewed: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
record.problems: Error outcomes are shown in figures without numeric values or uncertainty estimates. The error experiment uses 10% label noise; the cited 0% and 20% appendix plots show spectra only, so this does not establish behavior across the full corruption range.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying error rows identified. Appendix A Figure 8 shows spectra for 20% noise, not an error measure bearing on V4.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero total training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters relative to true-label training.
Training-time ratios for true versus random labels and convergence slowing across increasing corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect total training fit across corruption fractions and steadily increasing test error from clean to fully random labels. The reported error trajectories vary epochs at fixed corruption.
Controlled comparisons of weight decay, dropout, augmentation, and their removal for random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Comparisons between entirely true-labeled and entirely random-labeled datasets; the direct learning-order evidence uses partially corrupted datasets.

missing.what: The rows' descriptions omit the decisive early-phase comparison: test error falls rapidly while perturbed-label error remains high, before perturbed-label error subsequently falls. Add this timing information to the paired error rows.

record.verdict_notes: The main extraction error confuses variation across training epochs with variation across corruption fractions. Qualitative learning-order states follow the authors' explicit description, not reconstructed figure values. No model-specific differences in that ordering are stated.

versions.untested_parts: The study perturbs only 10% of training labels in its error plots; it does not test completely random labels or report the required comparison with unchanged training hyperparameters.
No comparison of training time for true versus random labels or convergence rate across corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.
The error plots report 10% label noise, not a sweep from no corruption through complete corruption; the text does not quantify perfect training fit across corruption fractions.
No experiments testing weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or their removal with random labels.
No test of whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: ResNet18

rows.note: The text says perturbed-set error decreases rapidly as training continues; the plotted value is not specified numerically.
rows.check: Interpret jointly with R2: perturbed-label error initially remains high while test error falls, then decreases during later memorization. Exact error values and perfect training fit cannot be established from the supplied figure text.
